title: Adjective Declension 4: Dative Singular
description: The dative singular for hard-stem adjectives. Masculine and neuter share -ому. The feminine reuses -ой (the same form as the genitive). Triggers: помогать, звонить, дать, нравиться, рад, the preposition к, age, and the impersonal 'мне холодно' family.
descriptionRussian: Дательный падеж единственного числа: мужской и средний делят окончание -ому, женский повторяет -ой (та же форма, что и в родительном).
intro: One new ending for the masculine and neuter, and nothing at all for the feminine, which keeps the form from last lesson. Worth noticing in passing: the masculine animate accusative borrowed from the genitive, but it does not borrow from the dative. That loan was a one-off, not a habit.
rules: Masculine and neuter share one dative singular ending: -ому. Hard-stem -ый and -ое both become -ому. Spelled -ому, pronounced /-omu/.
Feminine takes -ой in the dative singular, the same form as the feminine genitive. The trigger (verb / preposition / construction), not the form, decides the case.

Dative triggers: помогать / звонить / дать + dat, нравиться-style experiencer, рад / рада + dat, к + dat (motion toward a person), age constructions ('Маше 25 лет'), impersonal feelings ('мне холодно').

The masculine animate accusative borrowed the genitive -ого form, but it does NOT borrow the dative -ому. Three distinct masculine forms appear across acc / gen / dat: нового брата (acc), нет нового брата (gen), помогаю новому брату (dat).
examples: Я помогаю новому брату. (I help my new brother.) Брат masc: новый → новому.
Я звоню старой маме. (I am calling old mom.) Мама fem: старая → старой. Same form as the genitive 'у старой мамы'.
Маша рада новому письму. (Masha is glad about the new letter.) Письмо neut: новое → новому. Same -ому as the masculine.
Антон идёт к старому учителю. (Anton is going to the old teacher.) 'К + dat': старый → старому, учитель → учителю.
Умной сестре двадцать лет. (The smart sister is twenty years old.) Age: experiencer is dative. Сестра fem: умная → умной.
Маленькому мальчику холодно. (The little boy is cold.) Impersonal feeling: experiencer is dative. Мальчик masc: маленький → маленькому.

tables.title: Three Cases of новый брат: Compare

items.promptEnglish: I don't have a new magazine.
items.hint: Recap from Lesson 3: 'нет' triggers which case? Журнал is masculine.
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 3. 'У меня нет' triggers the genitive. Журнал is masculine: новый → нового. Today's drill, starting Q1.2, switches to the dative.

items.promptEnglish: Masha is glad about the new letter.
items.hint: 'Рад / рада + dat'. Письмо is neuter. Does the neuter take its own ending in the dative?
items.explanation: 'Рад / рада' takes a dative complement. Письмо is neuter; from the genitive onward neuter shares with masculine: -ому → новому. The same -ому would also fit a masculine noun (рада новому брату).

items.promptEnglish: Anton is going to the old teacher.
items.hint: 'К + dat' for motion toward a person. Учитель is masc.
items.explanation: 'К + dat' triggers the dative. Учитель is masculine, so старый → старому. Note учитель ends in soft -ь but its dative is hard -ю → учителю; the adjective ends in hard -ому regardless of the noun's softness.

blanks: Маленькому _____ холодно. (The little boy is cold.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Impersonal feeling phrases ('кому холодно / весело / грустно') put the experiencer in the dative. Мальчик is masculine: + -у → мальчику. The adjective in the question is already in the dative (маленькому); the noun follows the same case.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I often help my little brother.
errorCorrection.explanation: Помогать governs the dative, so the adjective takes the masculine dative ending -ому: маленькому брату. Маленького is the genitive and animate-accusative form (я знаю маленького брата), a natural slip because the stem is the same.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: In the evening Masha calls her old friend.
errorCorrection.explanation: Звонить governs the dative, and the feminine dative ending is -ой: старой подруге. Старую is the feminine ACCUSATIVE (Маша видит старую подругу), a natural slip if you treat the person called as a direct object, but звонить takes a recipient in the dative, not an object. The feminine -ой here is the same form as the feminine genitive from Lesson 3.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Anton is very glad about the interesting letter.
errorCorrection.explanation: The short adjective рад governs the dative, and from the genitive onward the neuter shares the masculine ending, so -ое becomes -ому: интересному письму. Интересное is the nominative/accusative neuter form, correct only for a subject or direct object.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Masha is glad about the new book.
minimalPairs.explanation: 'Рад / рада' takes the dative. Книга is feminine, so the dative ending is -ой: новой. Новую would be the accusative form ('Маша читает новую книгу').

reviewVocab.definition: dative case (marks the recipient or experiencer; answers 'Кому?')
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Я помогаю новому брату' слова 'новому' и 'брату' стоят в дательном падеже.

reviewVocab.definition: recipient (the person who receives an action: помогать кому, звонить кому, дать что-то кому)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Я звоню старому другу' слово 'другу' обозначает получателя звонка.

reviewVocab.definition: experiencer (the person whose age, feeling, or state is being described; goes in the dative)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Умной сестре двадцать лет' умной сестре — переживающий, поэтому стоит в дательном падеже.
